taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## 1. BY PRIMARY MECHANIC

### 1.1 Loop / Path Drawing
*The solver draws a continuous line or loop through the grid.*

#### 1.1.1 Single Loop (Hamiltonian-style)
- **Masyu** – loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** – loop drawn on dot grid edges, constrained by numeric cell clues
- **Yajilin** – loop avoids black cells; arrow-number clues indicate black cell counts
- **Mid-loop** – loop passes through black circles at the midpoint of straight segments
- **Dotchi-Loop** – loop through white circles (all straight or all turning per region); avoids black circles
- **Moon-or-Sun** – loop alternates between visiting moon cells and sun cells across rooms
- **Nagareru** – directional loop obeying wind constraints from arrow cells
- **Suraromu** – loop starts/ends at numbered circle, must cross all gates in order

#### 1.1.2 Path Connection (Non-loop)
- **Numberlink** – connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – connect island-nodes with 1–2 bridges; all islands connected; no crossings

---

### 1.2 Cell Shading / Painting
*The solver determines which cells are black (shaded) and which are white.*

#### 1.2.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** – white islands of given size; continuous black wall; no 2×2 black
- **Nurimisaki** – white promontory (misaki) cells with numbered reach; no 2×2 black or white
- **Heyawake** – rooms with shaded-cell counts; no adjacent shaded cells; white cells connected; white can't span 3+ rooms in a line
- **Kurodoko** – numbered cells count visible white cells; black cells non-adjacent; white connected
- **Kurotto** – circled numbers = sum of adjacent black cell groups; circles stay white
- **Norinori** – exactly two shaded cells per region, each forming a domino
- **LITS** – one tetromino per region; all shaded connected; no 2×2 shaded; same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent
- **Usowan** – numbers count adjacent shaded cells (one lie per room); shaded non-adjacent; white connected
- **Nurimeizu** – rooms entirely shaded or white; create maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles off it; no 2×2
- **Nuritwin** – each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2; twin blocks non-adjacent within region

#### 1.2.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – black groups must be rectangles/squares; white groups must NOT be rectangles/squares; numbers give area
- **Shakashaka** – place diagonal half-black triangles; remaining white areas must form rectangles; numbers count adjacent triangles
- **Tilepaint** – entire tiles shaded or unshaded; diagonal-cell numbers constrain row/column black counts

#### 1.2.3 Shading with Gravity / Physical Simulation
- **Sto-stone** – shade connected groups in rooms; groups can't connect across room borders; when "dropped" they fill the bottom half exactly

#### 1.2.4 Elimination Shading
- **Hitori** – shade duplicate numbers so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded non-adjacent; white connected

---

### 1.3 Region Division / Partitioning
*The solver divides the grid into regions (blocks) satisfying constraints.*

#### 1.3.1 Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** – partition into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### 1.3.2 Polyomino Partitioning
- **Five Cells** – partition into pentominoes; numbers count surrounding block edges (including frame)
- **Double Choco** – partition into blocks where each block has a matching white and gray sub-region of identical shape

#### 1.3.3 L-shaped / Special-shape Partitioning
- **Sashigane** – partition into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark endpoints; numbers give block size

---

### 1.4 Number Placement / Fill-in
*The solver places numbers in cells according to arithmetic or positional rules.*

#### 1.4.1 Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition

#### 1.4.2 Region-based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – fill grid with numbers; connected same-number groups have size = that number; same-size groups non-adjacent
- **Ripple Effect** – each room gets 1 to N; same numbers in a row/column must be spaced ≥ that number apart
- **Makaro** – rooms filled 1 to N; arrows in black cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms

#### 1.4.3 Crossword-style Number Fill
- **Nansuke** – place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-like grid

---

### 1.5 Object Placement
*The solver places specific objects (light bulbs, snakes, pencils, etc.) into the grid.*

#### 1.5.1 Light/Illumination Placement
- **Akari** – place light bulbs; each illuminates its row/column to the nearest wall; all white cells lit; no bulb illuminates another; numbered walls constrain adjacent bulb count

#### 1.5.2 Directional / Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** – place snakes (1–5 sequences) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight attack rule from head direction
- **Pencils** – identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips; pencil numbers give length; line length = pencil number
- **Evolomino** – place growing polyomino blocks along arrows; each successive block adds one square without rotation

#### 1.5.3 Movement-based Placement
- **Satogaeri** – move numbered circles within countries so each country has exactly one; circles move exact distances; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – move all circles straight into gray areas; arrows can't cross; gray area numbers = sum of entering circle values

---

### 1.6 Symbol / Mark Placement
*The solver fills cells with non-numeric symbols.*

- **Juosan** – fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain majority symbol; no 3+ consecutive same symbols in restricted direction
- **Chained Block** – fill cells black or white forming blocks; each block contains one number (= block size) or ?; blocks chain diagonally; no duplicate block shape within a chain

---

## 2. BY CONSTRAINT TYPE (Cross-cutting)

### 2.1 Numeric Clues
| Constraint Style | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Count of adjacent objects** | Akari, Shakashaka, Slitherlink, Kurotto, Usowan, Five Cells |
| **Count in a direction/region** | Yajilin, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Tilepaint, Juosan |
| **Size of containing region** | Shikaku, Fillomino, Choco Banana, Sashigane, Chained Block, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Sto-stone |
| **Sequence / position** | Ripple Effect, Makaro, Hebi, Suraromu |
| **Sum / total** | Yosenabe, Kurotto |
| **Distance moved** | Satogaeri |
| **Latin square** | Sudoku, Hitori |

### 2.2 Connectivity Constraints
| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **White cells connected** | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Hitori, Usowan, Nurimeizu |
| **Black/shaded cells connected** | LITS, Nuritwin, Sto-stone |
| **No 2×2 same-color block** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin |
| **Shaded cells non-adjacent** | Heyawake, Hitori, Usowan, Yajilin |
| **Single connected loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Yajilin, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu |
| **Connected bridge network** | Hashiwokakero |

### 2.3 Visibility / Line-of-sight
- Akari (bulb illumination), Kurodoko (white cell count to wall), Hebi (snake attack sight line), Nurimisaki (white line from promontory)

### 2.4 Shape Constraints
| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Rectangles required** | Shikaku, Choco Banana (black), Shakashaka (white areas) |
| **Rectangles forbidden** | Choco Banana (white) |
| **Specific polyominoes** | LITS (tetrominoes), Five Cells (pentominoes), Evolomino (growing polyominoes) |
| **L-shapes** | Sashigane |
| **Shape matching** | Double Choco, Nuritwin, Chained Block (uniqueness within chain) |

---

## 3. BY GRID ELEMENT USED

| Grid Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Dot grid (lines on edges)** | Slitherlink |
| **Cell-center paths/loops** | Masyu, Yajilin, Numberlink, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Pencils |
| **Bold-line regions (rooms)** | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Double Choco, Five Cells, Norinori, LITS, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Suraromu, Usowan, Satogaeri, Chained Block |
| **Circles (black/white)** | Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Hashiwokakero, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Nurimisaki, Kurotto, Sashigane, Mid-loop, Suraromu |
| **Arrows** | Makaro, Yajilin, Hebi, Sashigane, Nagareru, Evolomino, Yosenabe |
| **Colored/gray cells** | Double Choco, Sto-stone |
| **Pre-placed numbers** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Hitori, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Akari, Shakashaka, Shikaku, Choco Banana |

---

## 4. BY PUZZLE FAMILY / ORIGIN LINEAGE

| Family | Members |
|---|---|
| **Nuri- (painting) family** | Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Norinori |
| **Loop family** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Yajilin, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu |
| **Number-fill family** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke |
| **Shading/pattern family** | Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Usowan, LITS, Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint |
| **Region-division family** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Double Choco, Sashigane |
| **Connection family** | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero |
| **Movement/placement family** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Hebi, Evolomino, Pencils, Akari |
| **Block-shape family** | Chained Block, Choco Banana, LITS, Evolomino |

---
